checks: The base moment at zero gives σ_j,-1=σ_j,1 because the coarea factor is constant across bases for each cap. Normalization makes θ_jS_j proportional to ρ_j, so Σ_zT_z=0. Through-source offsets and base moments give Σ_zB_z=0, and common cap masses give Σ_zC_z=Q.

On a proper clipped trace, Gauss–Green gives the new face flux with outward normal -v_j/||v_j||, giving the stated signs of B_z and T_z. Saturated and surface-null supporting traces and counting measure in dimension one are handled. The maximizing center gives h_Kz(-T_z).

Endpoint hinges isolate actual exposed bases with a finite affine penalty. Their numerators attain the endpoint optima. Support addition and T_0=-2T give dQ+2G for the formal sum. Positive width of the actual Minkowski midpoint implies G>0 for T≠0.

The lifted center triangle is contained in the actual body. Its sections are exactly the indicated segment, including degenerate cases when the middle displacement is zero. For every n its support is a concave scalar function of z, and the displayed global extension has the same concavity. The resulting nonnegative convex field qualifies for roof realization.

At old measured boundary normals the positive part causes no extra clipping because the center section is inside each fiber. The total affine-center integral is dV. Its weighted integral is dQ since ΣB_z=0 and ΣT_z·f(z)=0. The middle correction is exactly (n·D)_+, producing J and L_+.
The endpoint terms make the denominator strictly positive. Constant-vector Gauss–Green gives ∫Wn=T_0 on the middle boundary, so L_+−L_-=−2T·D=−2G. Cross-multiplication yields the claimed criterion.
